source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Keep the client supine and elevate the legs to increase venous return without changing trunk position.","B":"Turn the client onto a side to relieve gravid-uterus compression of major vessels and restore venous return.","C":"Give a carbohydrate drink before repositioning because late-pregnancy supine dizziness usually reflects hypoglycemia.","D":"Continue the ultrasound with the client flat for several minutes and reposition if the dizziness fails to resolve spontaneously."}}
source_row.rationale: ACOG explains that lying flat in later pregnancy can allow the gravid uterus to compress a major vessel, reducing venous return and causing dizziness; turning to either side relieves the positional compression. Option B directly addresses the likely mechanism. Option A maintains the provoking position. Option C assumes hypoglycemia without evidence and does not first correct the positional cause. Option D delays the needed repositioning while the client remains symptomatic.

source_row.stem: A client in the third trimester becomes dizzy and nauseated while lying flat during an ultrasound. Which nursing action best addresses the likely cause?
